- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect pessimism or uncertainty.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >2.5x recent mean), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or apply decay to prevent runaway growth.  
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 2.5+ consecutive days above 2.40); add 0.1–0.3 to forecast to reflect reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; adjust final 5–7 days to match sentiment trend, especially if sentiment turns sharply.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/1.00 alternation, model tends to lag; add 0.1–0.2 to forecast for each such cycle to account for delayed reaction.  
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 0.1–0.2 to avoid overcorrection.
